newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr recovers after stumble over Japan surplus.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr recovers after stumble over Japan surplus.

text.p: The dollar recovered some poise in early European trade on Monday after stumbling briefly to 114.85 yen in Asian dealings because of a sharp jump in Japan's trade surplus.

In equities, which saw record closes in many European bourses on Friday, most markets were closed because of the Pentecost holiday. London, one of the few to open, fell at the start, depressed by Wall Street's big drop on Friday over interest rate worries ahead of a crucial meeting of the U.S. central bank's policy-making committee.

The dollar took fright at data early on Monday which showed Japan's overall trade surplus ballooned 163.7 percent to 831.48 billion yen ($7.2 billion) in April. Japan's sensitive surplus with the U.S also jumped 174.1 percent from a year earlier to 468.97 billion ($4.07 billion) yen.
But analysts said the impact on the dollar was likely to be short-lived.

"The numbers came in very close to expectations...The other interesting component is that exports were very strong but imports were not that weak," said Sean Shepley international economist CS First Boston.
The dollar clawed its way back to 116.02 yen after slumping to lows of 114.85 yen in Asia immediately after the data and compared with 115.53 yen in late Europe on Friday.
Against the mark, the dollar was virtually unchanged from the levels seen late on Friday and turnover was quiet because of the holiday.
Analysts said dollar markets were likely to remain subdued ahead of the U.S Federal Open Market Committee Meeting (FOMC) on Tuesday which will decide on U.S. interest rates.

In equities too, investors were worried about the FOMC's meeting and London's blue-chip FTSE 100 index fell a few points in sympathy with Wall Stret which tumbled nearly two percent on Friday because of interest rate jitters.
London hit its ninth closing high in the last 11 sessions, at 4,693.9 points, on Friday and traders said on Monday that a shortage of stock was helping to cap potential losses.

"Market makers would dearly love to take this market down quite a reasonable distance," said one dealer. "But market makers are also nervous of pulling a big mark-down in case they trigger more buying".
Many investors were growing nervous that the record-breaking perfromance of bourses would be vulnerable to any increase in interest rates in the influential U.S. economy.

"Some of the bravado that the market was feeling on the possibility that (U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan wouldn't put up rates is evaporating," said one equity salesman. "The market is now preparing itself for a quarter percent increase and anything different from that would really twitch us," he added.
STOCK PRICES AT 0930 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 12.9 points at 4,681.0.
Paris and Frankfurt were closed.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6950 marks and 116.02 yen compared with 1.6944 marks and 115.53 yen in late European trade on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $343.00 in early dealings versus London's close of $344.75 on Friday. Silver was at $4.69, down two cents.
